item.title: Who Should Own AI? Building Public AI — Sat Nov 21, 2:00 PM — North York Central Library
item.description: If AI becomes as important as roads, electricity, or libraries, who should own it? Who decides what it's used for? Who gets access and to say no? This panel discussion, as part of our Innovator-in-Residence program with Ryan Kelln , will include speakers building public-interest AI, working in civic tech, and organizing communities affected by AI decisions. We'll explore what's already being built, from open models and public compute to community-owned data, and what's being privatized. You'll get to draft your own "public AI requirements" and see what others think should be guaranteed to everyone. The future of AI is being decided now; this is a chance to have a say in it. Featuring: Alex Olson , Director of University of Toronto’s Centre for Analytics & AI Engineering Khasir Hean , Steward of Technologists for Democracy, Machine Learning Nathalie Claire DiBerardino , Project Lead, DARO Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM. item.title: Get Things Done with AI: Build Your Own Productivity System — Mon Nov 23, 4:00 PM — North York Central Library
item.description: What if your to-do list could check in on you, notice what's been stuck for weeks, and offer to help instead of just sitting there? In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence, Ryan Kelln , you'll explore a personal productivity system built around an AI agent and a weekly-review practice. See how the agent loads goals, counts what actually got done, flags the items that keep slipping, and drafts next week's plan. It can support without cheerleading, asking "Why has this been stuck for three weeks? Here are your options." You'll try it yourself with a practice set of goals, and leave with the plain-text templates and a clearer map of how an AI might support you, ready to build your own system at home. Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required. Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM. item.description: On November 24 th , join Homeless Connect Toronto at the Toronto Reference Library for a special premiere screening and community conversation celebrating the launch of Seeking Shelter, a documentary series by filmmaker Nadine Valcin. As Canada continues to grapple with a growing housing crisis, Seeking Shelter shines a light on the people, organizations, and grassroots movements creating innovative and inclusive solutions to housing instability. item.title: Book Launch: That Directionless Light of the Future, Rediscovering Russell FitzGerald — Thu Nov 26, 5:00 PM — Art Metropole
item.description:

That Directionless Light of the Future: Rediscovering Russell FitzGerald is the first major publication devoted to artist Russell FitzGerald. Bringing together newly commissioned scholarship and more than 90 reproductions of paintings, drawings, illustrations, archival material the book offers the first comprehensive account of an artist whose ambitious vision has remained hidden for decades.
Edited by Canadian art historian and curator Jon Davies, this handsome volume brings together reproductions of the artist’s work and other material with new texts by Davies, Dodie Bellamy, and Jamie Parra to return FitzGerald to art history and consider his relevance to the present.
For further information, visit our website.

item.title: Geometric Art and Watercolours — Sat Nov 28, 10:00 AM — Richview
item.description:
Geometric patterns are among the most recognizable visual expressions of Islamic art and architecture. In the past, craftsmen had an extensive practical knowledge of geometry. Nowadays, we tend to rely heavily on tools such as a protractors, compasses, and rulers. In this workshop, participants will be guided through step-by-step instructions using drawing tools and watercolour paint to create their own geometric pattern and complex design art pieces. item.title: Public AI: What Should We Build Together? — Sat Nov 28, 10:00 AM — Toronto Reference Library
item.description:
What would AI look like if it were designed to serve the public, much like our libraries? This interactive workshop invites you to imagine AI as a public resource, one that is accessible to everyone, accountable to the people it serves, and developed with the public interest in mind. Join us to share your experiences, imagine new possibilities and help shape a vision for Public AI in Canada. This workshop is part of TPL's AI Summit and presented by Public AI Lab Canada in collaboration with DemocracyXChange.
